key_insight: The paper establishes a calibration-focused in-situ thermal XRD workflow to more accurately measure true sample temperature and phase stability in cesium halide perovskite powders.
engineering_relevance: This improves how high-temperature stability is assessed for perovskite solar-cell materials, helping researchers avoid misleading phase-transition and decomposition temperatures caused by furnace/sample temperature mismatch.
method: Used CsPbCl3 as a baseline model inorganic perovskite to validate the thermal-testing methodology.
Applied in-situ temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction to track phase transitions and decomposition onsets.
Extended the same approach to the double perovskite Cs2AgSbCl6 to probe thermal kinetics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stoichiometry/phase and morphology analysis plus temperature conversions on a control substrate, with in-situ XRD used to identify phase transitions and decomposition temperatures.
watch_item: High-temperature results depend strongly on accurate temperature calibration and sample preparation, so substrate effects and measurement reproducibility must be tightly controlled.
paper_title: Thermal Corrections and Analysis on the Phase Stability of CsPbCl3 and Cs2AgSbCl6 during In-Situ Thermal Treatment
